chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Abi al-Suhban, from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ribat, from Sa'id al-A'raj who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I fasted the day concerning which there is doubt, and it turned out to be from the month of Ramadan — shall I make it up?' He said: 'No, it is a day for which you were granted divine success (tawfiq).'

key_terms.شَهْرُ رَمَضَانَ: The month of Ramadan — the obligatory fasting month in the Islamic calendar
key_terms.قَضَاء: Make-up fast — obligation to compensate for a missed Ramadan fast on another day
key_terms.وُفِّقْتَ: Tawfiq — being granted divine success or guidance; here indicates the fast was accepted by God
key_terms.يَوْمَ الشَّكِّ: Day of doubt — the final day of Sha'ban when the sighting of the Ramadan crescent is uncertain

ai.seo_question: Do I need to make up the fast I kept on the day of doubt if it turns out to be Ramadan?
ai.summary: Sa'id al-A'raj asked Imam al-Sadiq (AS) whether he needed to make up a fast observed on the 'day of doubt' (yawm al-shakk) — the last day of Sha'ban when it is uncertain if Ramadan has begun — after it turned out to be the first day of Ramadan. The Imam ruled that no make-up (qada') is required. The ruling reflects a jurisprudential principle: when a believer acts in good faith based on available evidence and is later confirmed to have acted correctly, the act is deemed valid and accepted. The phrase 'a day for which you were granted tawfiq' implies divine guidance and approval of the act performed.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Abu Al Suhban, from Ali Bin Al Husayn Bin Rabaat, from Saeed Al a’araj who said,

‘I said to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, ‘I Fast the day wherein is a doubt, so it turns out to be from the Month of Ramaan. Shall I fulfil (make up for it)?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No, it is a day commensurate for it’.
en.sarwar: 4. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn abu al-Suhban from Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ribat from Sa‘id al-’A‘raj who has said the following:

“I once asked Abu `Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ’I have fasted on the day which is doubtful about its being of al-Sha £ ban or of the month of Ramadan, if there is Qada’ (compensatory fast) upon me.’ He (the Imam) said, £ No, Qada’ (compensatory fast) is not obligatory on you and it was a day in which you had a fortunate chance.’”
